opening_message:
Ticket 1: Keith Mclaughlin (employee ID E032) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E032.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Keith Mclaughlin (E032) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Source Code. Full-time employees qualify for up to write access; admin is only for the owning role (Engineer), so write is the maximum allowed. Requested level (write) equals the maximum, so recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security record for E032 shows contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Contractors max is read unless they have advanced training (never admin). Requested write exceeds maximum, so recommend granting read.
reason: The two notes conflict on Keith Mclaughlin's (E032) employment type: HR notes full_time (max write), while the Security record indicates contractor with basic security training (max read, since contractors only get write with advanced training, never admin). Given the conflicting facts and the request for write access, I apply the more restrictive, security-verified classification. Contractor with basic training cannot exceed read, so the granted level is read.

The Approver reads the notes and makes the final decision. Notes may conflict; we have to decide with the information available.

Given conflicting facts, I'd lean toward the security agent's data being more authoritative for contractor status since security determines contractor status and training. Also security training: basic -> read max. So grant read.

Actually wait — which agent is which? Note 1 says "role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)" - that's likely HR (they look up role/employment).
